title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page does not belong to the De Rham / divided-power notes around it. It is a typed page, numbered '- 29 -' and headed 'IX', from Grothendieck's Exposé IX of SGA 7 I, 'Modèles de Néron et monodromie', §3 on semi-abelian reduction. The neighbouring pages are handwritten notes on the automorphism group scheme Ω of the divided-power De Rham complex; this page has nothing to do with them and was presumably misfiled in cote 136.

Mathematical content, step by step.

(1) End of the proof of a lemma (3.1). The lemma concerns a commutative group scheme K over S with special point s and generisation t. The step uses a reduction to S local, noetherian and complete, and invokes SGA 3 XV 1.6 c), X 3.2, IX 3.6 and IX 5.2. It establishes (3.1.4.1): rang mult(nK_s) divides rang mult(nK_t) for every n ≥ 1.
- 'rang mult' is the rank (in effect, the order) of the largest subgroup of multiplicative type of the algebraic group, as in SGA 3 XVII 7.2.1.
- The text notes that a torsion algebraic group of multiplicative type is finite, so these ranks are finite numbers.
- So the multiplicative part of the n-torsion can only shrink under specialisation, in the sense of divisibility.
- Via the unipotence criterion SGA 3 XVII 4.6.1 (vi), this gives part c): if K_t is unipotent, so is K_s.

(2) Proposition 3.2. Setting: S is a locally noetherian, regular, integral scheme of dimension 1 with function field K; A_K is an abelian variety over K; A is its Néron model, smooth and separated over S, and quasi-projective when S is noetherian (citation [23] = Raynaud, Faisceaux amples, VIII). The following are equivalent:
- (i) for every s, A_s^0 has unipotent rank 0, i.e. A_s^0 is an extension of an abelian variety by a torus (semi-abelian reduction everywhere);
- (ii) there exists some smooth, separated, finite-type group scheme G over S extending A_K whose fibres have unipotent rank 0.
Moreover, for any such G, the morphism G → A given by the Néron mapping property is an open immersion onto an open subgroup, so G^0 ≅ A^0.

Role: this is the step that reduces the semi-stable reduction theorem to producing *some* semi-abelian smooth model, for example from a semi-stable curve or a Raynaud-type construction. Its key input is the specialisation behaviour of multiplicative and unipotent ranks proved just above.
errors: Typographical only. The parenthesis in '(SGA 3 VII 1.1, il en est de même' is not closed.
No mathematical errors. The page is the published SGA 7 text.

ideas.what: Specialisation of the multiplicative rank of n-torsion of fibres of a commutative group scheme: rang mult(nK_s) divides rang mult(nK_t); hence unipotence of the generic fibre passes to the special fibre.
ideas.modern_name: Semicontinuity of toric/unipotent rank under specialisation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck, SGA 7 I Exp. IX §3 (building on SGA 3)

ideas.what: Characterisation of semi-abelian reduction: the Néron model has semi-abelian identity component iff some smooth separated finite-type model with semi-abelian fibres exists, and any such model embeds as an open subgroup of the Néron model (G^0 ≅ A^0).
ideas.modern_name: Semi-abelian (semistable) reduction criterion; open immersion of semi-abelian models into the Néron model
ideas.where_published: SGA 7 I, Exposé IX, Prop. 3.2; also Bosch–Lütkebohmert–Raynaud, Néron Models §7.4

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typed page of the published SGA 7 Exposé IX (Néron models and monodromy), apparently misfiled among the 1976 De Rham divided-power notes. Its content is standard and is published and credited to Grothendieck. The only point of interest is archival: the page is misplaced in the archive.
transcription_corrections: The page is a typescript of SGA 7 I, Exp. IX, p. 29, not part of the handwritten De Rham notes. '347' is the archive stamp, and '178' (bottom left) is the folder page number.
'schéma abélien sur K' is as typed (A_K an abelian scheme over Spec K).
The transcription is otherwise accurate. Missing ')' after 'SGA 3 VII 1.1' and missing '3' in 'SGA XVII 4.6.1' are present in the original.
